notes: TECH APPROVED (maintainer 2026-09-07): Firestore, Standard/Native mode, single region europe-north1, reached ONLY server-side via @google-cloud/firestore. NO Firebase SDK in the client, NO security rules, NO Firebase Auth — Firestore is the database, Firebase is a platform we do not use. Three reasons the line is absolute: a client that can write the database directly can write its own inventory and the server is authoritative; the Firebase client SDK is hundreds of KB into a bundle that ships none of it; and Firebase Auth is precisely the auth aggregator the maintainer was right to refuse in his first message.

SIMPLICITY CORRECTION the maintainer forced, kept as law because it was a real over-build: I proposed EdDSA/JWT signed tokens + jose + Secret Manager so identity could be verified WITHOUT a database read — then the join already reads the account document for level and inventory, so the whole crypto layer bought nothing. Identity is {accountId, secret}: server-minted, compared timing-safe against a hash on the account doc during the read that was already happening. Revocation is rotating a field; multi-process needs no key distribution; zero crypto libraries. GENERAL RULE FOR THIS DOMAIN: separate decisions that cost nothing (naming, data shape, when to write) from technology that costs something (packages, services, ops). Only the second pile is bloat, and it is currently ONE package.

REGION: europe-north1, NOT the eur3 multi-region I first proposed. Multi-region storage under single-region compute buys availability that cannot be used — a europe-north1 outage takes Cloud Run with it and the game is down either way. Cheaper, lower latency, same region as the rest of the stack.

COST, measured 2026-09-07 (us-central1 rates, EU somewhat higher): reads $0.03/100k, writes $0.09/100k, deletes $0.01/100k, storage ~$0.144/GiB/month. Free daily: 50,000 reads / 20,000 writes / 20,000 deletes / 1 GiB — for the (default) database only, one per project (this project has never used Firebase, so the allowance is unclaimed). Firestore has no instance, node or minimum, so idle is unbilled: development costs nothing at ~0.1% of the free tier. PITR and scheduled backups stay OFF — they bill per GiB and dev data is disposable under the no-migration law.

DATABASE LIVE 2026-09-07, created by the maintainer from Cloud Shell on a phone: projects/nagijala/databases/(default), europe-north1, FIRESTORE_NATIVE, freeTier true, PITR disabled. NOTE THE PROJECT ID IS 'nagijala' — one n, it does not match the game's name. Full record and the flags that matter in account/README.md.

TRAP, paid for: `gcloud config get-value project` prints '(unset)' and EXITS 0, so a `cmd && cmd` Cloud-Shell chain runs straight past a missing project and dies one step later with an unrelated-looking error. games2/deploy/ar-cleanup.sh and .github/gcs-backup-bootstrap.sh already carry the correct derivation and the [ "$PROJECT_ID" = "(unset)" ] guard — reuse them, never hand-roll it. I hand-rolled it and cost the maintainer a round trip.

PHASE 1 SHIPPED 2026-09-07. Every player is now GIVEN an account silently on the join call the client already makes — entry is still one tap, nothing about the select screen changed. Code at games2/server/src/account/store.ts (NOT a top-level games2/account/: the runtime image copies games2/shared, games2/server and games2/config only, so a top-level module would typecheck, test, build green and then be MISSING in production). Deleted: server/src/store.ts, server/test/store.test.ts, client getPlayerToken()/'ml-token', every 'saved?.' migration fallback in onJoin, and the synchronous whole-file write on the game loop. Verified: server suite 468 tests / 442 pass / 25 fail — the SAME 25 that were already failing on main before I touched anything (missing tiles art, e.g. tiles/tops/brown_paving_stone/.../tile_05.36000560.webp), zero introduced. All three tsconfigs clean.

TRAP CAUGHT BEFORE SHIPPING, worth the whole test run: the server first PUSHED the minted {id,secret} from onJoin, and a message sent from onJoin can arrive BEFORE the client has registered its handler. The failure is silent and total — the pair is dropped, so the browser becomes a brand-new player on every visit, which is precisely the bug this domain exists to end. It is now PULLED: the client registers its handler, sends 'account:want', and the server answers only for a join that actually minted one. Never push identity from onJoin.

COST OF THE ONE DEPENDENCY, measured: @google-cloud/firestore pulls 73 packages / ~15 MB of node_modules (firestore + google-gax + grpc) and costs 89 ms of import at cold start. Server-side only — it never touches the client bundle. A zero-dependency alternative exists (Firestore's REST API + a metadata-server token, ~50 lines) and was rejected: this sits on the critical path of every player's join, and the maintainer's own rule for this layer is that a dependency here must be rock solid. Google's official client is that; my hand-rolled auth-refresh and retry logic would not be.
